mainTopic: Lessons from the יוסף story, verses near the end of מגילת אסתר (including the ten sons of המן), and the greatness of תלמוד תורה.
overview: This עמוד finishes the גמרא's lessons from the יוסף story and then returns to explaining the last chapters of מגילת אסתר. First, יוסף's extra garments for בנימין are explained as a hint to מרדכי's five royal garments, not favoritism. The tears at the brothers' reunion hint at the destruction of the two בתי מקדש and משכן שילה. Several verses then show יוסף reassuring his brothers and honoring his father, along with the saying 'bow to the fox in its hour.' Back in the מגילה, רב יהודה reads 'אורה ושמחה וששון ויקר' as תורה, יום טוב, מילה and תפילין. The גמרא gives rules for the ten sons of המן: they are read in one breath, the ו of ויזתא is written long, and their list is laid out like a falling wall. More verses are explained: the מלאך who slapped אחשורוש, אסתר's request, שרטוט for a מגילה, and the fasts sharing in establishing פורים. The עמוד ends with statements that תלמוד תורה is greater than saving lives, building the בית המקדש, and honoring parents. The last proof continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Why would יוסף repeat the mistake of favoritism?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge. Favoritism through clothing caused the brothers' jealousy, so how could יוסף give בנימין extra garments?
steps.simpleTranslation: Should he stumble in that very thing? After all, רב said: because of two סלעים' weight of fine wool that יעקב gave יוסף beyond his brothers, events rolled on and our forefathers went down to מצרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes a challenge against יוסף for giving בנימין five sets of clothing while the other brothers got one each. It backs the challenge with רב's teaching that a small act of favoritism led to the whole exile in מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף personally suffered because his father favored him with a special coat. So it seems impossible that he would repeat the same favoritism with בנימין. רב's statement shows how serious this is: a tiny gift of fine wool set off the chain of events that ended in exile.

keyTerms.meaning: He will stumble, meaning make the same mistake
Selaim, a unit of weight and coinage
Fine wool, used for יוסף's special coat
The matter rolled on, one event leading to the next

steps.confusionAlert: This עמוד starts in the middle of a sentence. The first half of the question, 'Is it possible that the very thing that צדיק suffered from…', appears on the previous עמוד. It refers to יוסף giving בנימין five changes of clothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב's teaching is a classic source for the practical rule that a parent should not favor one child over the others.

phrases.english: should he stumble in it?
phrases.notes: End of the question that began on the previous amud

phrases.english: As Rava bar Meḥaseyya said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
Because of the weight of two sela of fine wool
that Jacob gave Joseph beyond the rest of his brothers
the matter progressed and our forefathers went down to Egypt.

steps.triggerLanguage: יִכָּשֵׁל בּוֹ? דְּאָמַר רָבָא בַּר מַחְסֵיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began earlier
steps.kashyaTarget: יוסף's giving of five garments to בנימין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יוסף knew firsthand the damage favoritism causes, so he would not repeat it.

steps.title: The five garments hinted at מרדכי
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנימין בר יפת answers that the five garments were not favoritism. They were a hint that מרדכי, a descendant of בנימין, would wear five royal garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי בנימין בר יפת said: he was giving him a hint that a descendant would come from him who would leave the king's presence in five royal garments, as it says, 'And מרדכי went out in royal clothing of blue…'
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered. יוסף's gift was a prophetic hint, not favoritism.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the gift is understood as a sign of the future, the worry about jealousy disappears. The verse in אסתר lists five items: blue, white, a gold crown, a linen wrap, and purple. Each matches one of the five garments.

keyTerms.meaning: מרדכי, from the tribe of בנימין

steps.whatToRemember: The extra garments given to בנימין were a hint to מרדכי's five royal garments, not favoritism.

phrases.english: Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said:
He gave him a hint,
that a descendant was destined to come from him,
who would go out from before the king
in five royal garments,
as it is stated: 'And Mordecai went out'
in royal apparel of sky blue, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִן בַּר יֶפֶת: רֶמֶז רָמַז לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the act's purpose as a prophetic hint
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The garments were favoritism toward בנימין
steps.terutzMaskana: The garments hinted at מרדכי's five royal garments

steps.title: Why does the verse say בנימין's 'necks'?
steps.stepSummary: The verse uses the plural 'necks' for בנימין, and the גמרא asks how many necks he had.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he fell on the necks of בנימין his brother.' How many necks did בנימין have?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by noticing an odd plural word in the verse. It is setting up a דרש (an interpretation) in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word צַוְּארֵי is plural, but a person has only one neck. The unusual wording signals a hidden meaning.

phrases.english: 'And he fell upon his brother Benjamin's necks.'
How many necks did Benjamin have?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new verse-based teaching

steps.title: יוסף wept over the two בתי מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the plural hints at the two בתי מקדש. They would stand in בנימין's territory and be destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: he cried over two Sanctuaries destined to be in בנימין's portion and destined to be destroyed.
steps.whatsHappening: The question about the plural is answered: יוסף was crying over the two future Temples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each 'neck' stands for one מקדש. The neck is a fitting symbol, since the מקדש stood in בנימין's land, like a neck between the shoulders.

keyTerms.meaning: Sanctuaries, meaning the two בתי מקדש

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
He wept over two Temples
that were destined to be in Benjamin's territory
and were destined to be destroyed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: בָּכָה עַל שְׁנֵי מִקְדָּשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural hints at the two בתי מקדש in בנימין's land, which would be destroyed

steps.title: בנימין wept over שילה
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the verse, 'בנימין wept on his necks,' refers to משכן שילה. It stood in יוסף's territory and was destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And בנימין wept on his necks': he cried over משכן שילה, destined to be in יוסף's portion and destined to be destroyed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רבי אלעזר's reading with the second half of the same verse. Now בנימין cries for יוסף's loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is mirrored. Each brother wept over the Sanctuary that would be destroyed in the other's land. שילה was in the territory of אפרים, יוסף's son.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tabernacle at Shiloh, which stood before the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The brothers' tears at their reunion hinted at future destruction. יוסף wept for the two בתי מקדש, and בנימין wept for משכן שילה.

phrases.english: 'And Benjamin wept on his necks' —
he wept over the Tabernacle of Shiloh,
that was destined to be in Joseph's territory
and was destined to be destroyed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי אלעזר's reading to the second half of the verse
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בנימין's weeping refers to the destruction of משכן שילה in יוסף's land

steps.title: יוסף holds no grudge, just as with בנימין
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains why יוסף mentioned בנימין's eyes. Just as he had no resentment toward בנימין, who was not involved in selling him, he had none toward the other brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother בנימין.' רבי אלעזר said: יוסף told them, just as I hold nothing in my heart against בנימין, who was not part of my sale, so I hold nothing against you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new verse. It explains why יוסף compared the brothers to בנימין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mentioning בנימין's eyes together with theirs seems unnecessary. רבי אלעזר reads it as an equation: yours are like his. Since בנימין was obviously innocent and resented by no one, the brothers are reassured that they too are forgiven.

keyTerms.meaning: I hold nothing in my heart, meaning no resentment

phrases.english: 'And behold, your eyes see,
and the eyes of my brother Benjamin.'
Rabbi Elazar said: He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין בְּלִבִּי עַל בִּנְיָמִין אָחִי,
phrases.english: Just as I have nothing in my heart against my brother Benjamin,
for he was not part of my sale,
so too I have nothing in my heart against you.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִנֵּה עֵינֵיכֶם רוֹאוֹת וְעֵינֵי אָחִי בִנְיָמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New verse, new teaching
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוסף assured his brothers he bore them no grudge, just as he bore none toward innocent בנימין

steps.title: My mouth matches my heart
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the verse, 'for my mouth is speaking to you,' is read as 'as my mouth is, so is my heart.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For it is my mouth that speaks to you': as my mouth is, so is my heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the end of the same verse as יוסף's promise that his words are sincere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words כִּי פִי are read as כְּפִי, 'like my mouth.' This adds that יוסף's reassurance was not just polite talk. His inner feelings matched his words.
steps.whatToRemember: יוסף reassured his brothers twice: he had no grudge, as with בנימין, and his words truly matched his heart.

phrases.english: 'That it is my mouth that speaks to you.'
As my mouth is, so is my heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues interpreting the same verse
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוסף's words were sincere: his heart matched his mouth

steps.title: What were 'the good things of מצרים'?
steps.stepSummary: The verse says יוסף sent his father donkeys carrying 'the good of מצרים' without saying what it was. The גמרא asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And to his father he sent likewise ten donkeys carrying the good of מצרים.' What is 'the good of מצרים'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new verse with a question about an unclear phrase. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse names a specific gift but gives no detail. The גמרא wants to know what this 'good' item was.

phrases.english: 'And to his father he sent in this manner
ten donkeys carrying the good things of Egypt.'
What is 'the good things of Egypt'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New verse, new question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What gift 'the good of מצרים' refers to

steps.title: Old wine for the elderly father
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that יוסף sent aged wine, which older people find pleasing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי בנימין בר יפת said in the name of רבי אלעזר: he sent him old wine, which pleases the minds of the elderly.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered: the 'good of מצרים' was old wine chosen especially for יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף picked a gift suited to his elderly father's needs and comfort. The gift shows how thoughtful he was in honoring his father.
steps.whatToRemember: 'The good of מצרים' was old wine, a gift chosen to suit יעקב's old age.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר יֶפֶת אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said that Rabbi Elazar said:
He sent him aged wine,
which the elderly find pleasing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'good of מצרים' was aged wine, pleasing to the elderly

steps.title: The brothers bow to יוסף: 'When the fox has its hour, bow to it'
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנימין בר יפת quotes רבי אלעזר: the brothers falling before יוסף shows the folk saying 'bow to the fox in its hour.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And his brothers also went and fell down before him.' רבי בנימין בר יפת said in the name of רבי אלעזר: This is what people mean when they say, 'When the fox is in its hour, bow down to it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a verse about the brothers bowing to יוסף after יעקב died. רבי אלעזר links it to a popular saying about bowing to whoever is in power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying teaches that when someone has power, even someone you would not normally respect, you must submit to him. רבי אלעזר applies it to the brothers bowing to יוסף. The next step will question whether this saying fits here.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (introduces a folk saying)
Fox (a lowly animal, a symbol of someone minor)
In its hour / when its time has come

phrases.english: "And his brothers also went and fell down before him."
Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said
that Rabbi Elazar said:
This is what people say:
A fox in its hour, bow down to it.
phrases.notes: Even a lowly figure who is in power must be respected

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר יֶפֶת אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of teachings by רבי אלעזר about יוסף and his family.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The brothers bowing to יוסף illustrates the saying 'bow to the fox in its hour.'

steps.title: Why call יוסף a fox compared to his brothers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: calling יוסף a 'fox' implies he was lower than his brothers. But in what way was he lower?
steps.simpleTranslation: A fox? In what way was he lesser than his brothers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the use of the fox saying. Calling יוסף a 'fox' next to his brothers suggests he was beneath them, which is not true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying only fits when the one in power is normally of lower standing than the one bowing. יוסף was not lower than his brothers; he was a צדיק and their equal or better. So the saying does not fit this verse.

keyTerms.meaning: His inferiority / how he was lesser

phrases.english: A fox?!
In what way was he lesser than his brothers?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the fit of the saying quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying the 'fox' saying to the brothers bowing to יוסף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A 'fox' means someone of lower standing. יוסף was not lower than his brothers, so the comparison is insulting and does not fit.

steps.title: The saying really refers to יעקב bowing to יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves the teaching to a different verse: יעקב bowing at the head of his bed in front of יוסף. A father bowing to his son fits the fox saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if this was said, it was said like this: On the verse 'And ישראל bowed at the head of the bed,' רבי בנימין בר יפת said in the name of רבי אלעזר: A fox in its hour, bow down to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying רבי אלעזר's teaching was really said about a different verse. In that verse יעקב bows to his son יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Compared to his father יעקב, יוסף really was the 'lesser' one, since he was the son. Even so, because יוסף was in power at that time, יעקב bowed to him. That is exactly what the fox saying describes.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (corrects which source a teaching belongs to)

steps.confusionAlert: The fox saying itself is repeated word for word. The only change is which verse it is attached to: not the brothers bowing, but יעקב bowing.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said:
"And Israel bowed upon the head of the bed"
phrases.notes: בראשית מז:לא, יעקב bowing toward יוסף

phrases.english: Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said
that Rabbi Elazar said:
A fox in its hour, bow down to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 11 by moving the teaching to a different verse.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-attribution: the teaching was originally said about a different verse.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The saying described the brothers bowing to יוסף, which would make יוסף lower than them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The saying describes יעקב bowing to יוסף. A son is 'lesser' than his father, yet he is in power, so the saying fits.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Bow to the fox in its hour' is attached to יעקב bowing to יוסף, not to the brothers bowing.

steps.title: יוסף comforts his brothers: ten lights and one light
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains how יוסף 'spoke to their hearts.' He said: ten lights could not put out one, so how could one put out ten?
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And he comforted them and spoke to their hearts.' רבי בנימין בר יפת said in the name of רבי אלעזר: This teaches that he told them words the heart accepts. He said: If ten lights could not put out one light, how can one light put out ten lights?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what יוסף actually said to calm his brothers' fear of revenge. He gave them a convincing argument that they could feel was true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ten brothers are the 'ten lights,' and יוסף is the 'one light.' All ten of them together could not destroy him. So it makes sense that he, one person, cannot and will not destroy all ten. The argument works like a קל וחומר (an argument from the stronger case to the weaker one).

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches (introduces what a verse teaches)
Accepted by the heart; convincing and calming

phrases.english: "And he comforted them and spoke to their hearts."
Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said
that Rabbi Elazar said:
This teaches that he said to them
words that are accepted by the heart:
Now if ten lights
could not put out one light,
how can one light
put out ten lights?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר יֶפֶת אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם דְּבָרִים שֶׁמִּתְקַבְּלִין עַל הַלֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching in the same series by רבי אלעזר about יוסף and his brothers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוסף calmed his brothers with a logical argument: ten could not harm one, so one cannot harm ten.

steps.title: Back to the מגילה: light, gladness, and joy mean תורה, יום טוב, and מילה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reads the words of the פסוק in אסתר as hints to מצוות. אורה is תורה, שמחה is יום טוב, and ששון is מילה. Each one is supported by a verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'The Jews had light, gladness, joy, and honor.' רב יהודה said: 'Light' means תורה, as it says, 'For a מצוה is a lamp and תורה is light.' 'Gladness' means יום טוב, as it says, 'And you shall be glad on your festival.' 'Joy' means מילה, as it says, 'I rejoice over Your word.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the יוסף stories and goes back to explaining מגילת אסתר. רב יהודה explains the first three words of the verse, each with a proof verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: המן had banned these מצוות, so after the miracle the Jews could practice them again. Each word is linked to a מצוה through a verse that uses the same or a related word: אור/תורה, שמחה/חג, ששון/'שש אנכי.' The fourth word, יקר, is explained next.

keyTerms.meaning: Gladness, read here as יום טוב
And so it says (introduces a supporting verse)

steps.confusionAlert: The verse sounds like it is describing feelings (light, happiness). רב יהודה reads each word as a specific מצוה the Jews were able to do again. The proof for ששון = מילה comes from דוד rejoicing over 'Your word,' which חז"ל understood as the מצוה of מילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how חז"ל read the joy of פורים: it was not only physical rescue but also a return to living a Torah life.

phrases.english: "The Jews had light and gladness and joy and honor."
Rav Yehuda said:
"Light": this is Torah,
and so it says:
"For a מצוה is a lamp and Torah is light."
"Gladness": this is the Festival,
and so it says:
"And you shall be glad on your Festival."
"Joy": this is circumcision,
and so it says:
"I rejoice over Your word."
phrases.notes: תהלים קיט:קסב, understood as דוד's joy over מילה

steps.triggerLanguage: ״לַיְּהוּדִים הָיְתָה אוֹרָה וְשִׂמְחָה וְשָׂשׂוֹן וִיקָר״. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about יוסף and goes back to verse-by-verse explanation of מגילת אסתר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אורה = תורה, שמחה = יום טוב, ששון = מילה; each is proven from a verse.

steps.title: Honor means תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's reading continues: the word 'ויקר' in the אסתר verse hints at תפילין. A פסוק from דברים supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And honor' means תפילין. As the verse says: 'All the peoples of the earth will see that the name of ה׳ is called upon you, and they will fear you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב יהודה's list from the last step. After אורה, שמחה and ששון, the last word 'ויקר' is explained as תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word in the verse 'ליהודים היתה אורה ושמחה וששון ויקר' hints at a מצוה that המן had stopped and that came back after his downfall. 'ויקר' means honor. The support verse shows that the Jews wear something that carries ה׳'s name, which makes the nations stand in awe of them. That honor comes from תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: And honor; the fourth word of the אסתר verse
Leather boxes holding פסוקים, worn on the arm and the head
'And so it says'; this phrase brings a supporting verse

phrases.english: "And honor" — these are tefillin,
and so it says:
"And all the peoples of the earth will see
that the name of ה׳ is called upon you
and they will be afraid of you",

steps.triggerLanguage: וִיקָר אֵלּוּ תְּפִלִּין וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the four-word reading that רב יהודה began in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ויקר' in the אסתר verse refers to תפילין, supported by 'כי שם ה׳ נקרא עליך'.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר says it means the head-tefillin
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר הגדול. He says the verse 'the name of ה׳ is called upon you' refers to the תפילין worn on the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר הגדול says: this verse means the תפילין on the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the support verse from the last step. The ברייתא shows that this verse really is about תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 claimed that 'שם ה׳ נקרא עליך' refers to תפילין. Someone could ask how we know that. The ברייתא gives an older source, רבי אליעזר הגדול, who already read the verse this way. He also makes it more exact: the verse means the head-תפילין, which everyone can see.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught in a ברייתא
רבי אליעזר the Great (רבי אליעזר בן הורקנוס), a תנא
The תפילין worn on the head

steps.whatToRemember: The four words אורה, שמחה, ששון, ויקר stand for תורה, יום טוב, מילה, and תפילין. These are the מצוות the Jews could keep again once המן fell.

phrases.english: And it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
These are the tefillin of the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 15 that the verse refers to תפילין.
steps.raayaObject: That 'שם ה׳ נקרא עליך' refers to תפילין
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי אליעזר הגדול

steps.title: The ten sons of המן are read in one breath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the verse about the ten sons of המן. רב אדא דמן יפו rules that the reader says all ten names and the word 'עשרת' in one breath, because they all died together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And פרשנדתא... the ten sons of המן.' רב אדא דמן יפו said: the ten sons of המן and the word 'ten' must be said in one breath. Why? Because all their souls left them at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: how to read the verse that lists המן's ten sons. רב אדא gives a practical rule for reading the מגילה and then explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is about how the names are read aloud. The reader may not stop to breathe between the names. The reason is a hint: reading them all at once matches how they all died at once.

keyTerms.meaning: The ten sons of המן (אסתר ט:ו-י)

steps.confusionAlert: 'In one breath' is a rule about reading aloud. It is not about how the names are written. The writing rules come next, in steps 18-20.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the common practice of reading the names of המן's sons in one breath during מגילה reading.

phrases.english: "And Parshandatha... the ten sons of Haman."
Rav Adda from Jaffa said:
"The ten sons of Haman" and the word "ten"
must be said in one breath,
what is the reason?
All of their souls went out together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the hints in 'ליהודים היתה אורה' to the next verses in the מגילה, which list המן's sons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names of the ten sons and 'עשרת' are read in one breath, because they died together.

steps.title: The ו of ויזתא is written long
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the ו in ויזתא is stretched long, like a ship's pole, because all ten sons were hanged on one pole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the ו of 'ויזתא' must be stretched out straight and long, like the steering pole of a ship. Why? Because all of them were hanged on one pole.
steps.whatsHappening: A second rule about the ten sons. This one is about how the מגילה is written, not how it is read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא gave a reading rule in step 17. רבי יוחנן adds a writing rule: the letter ו in the last name, ויזתא, is drawn extra long. The long, straight letter looks like the single pole on which all the sons were hanged together.

keyTerms.meaning: Vaizatha, the tenth son of המן
An upright pole, or a stake used for hanging
A ship's steering pole or oar

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The vav of "Vaizatha"
must be stretched out like an upright pole
like the steering pole of a ship.
What is the reason?
They were all hanged on one pole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a writing rule for the same verse, alongside the reading rule from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ו of ויזתא is written long, to show that all ten sons were hanged on one pole.

steps.title: How songs in תנ״ך are normally laid out
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא quotes רבי שילא: every שירה in תנ״ך is written like a brick wall, with text placed over blank space and blank space placed over text.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפא said that רבי שילא of the village of כפר תמרתא taught: all the songs are written as a half-brick over a whole brick, and a whole brick over a half-brick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It first states the normal rule for writing songs, so that the exception about המן's sons will make sense in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An 'אריח' (half-brick) is a piece of written text. A 'לבינה' (whole brick) is a blank space. In a normal שירה, such as אז ישיר, the lines alternate, so text sits over blank space like bricks in a strong wall.

keyTerms.meaning: Songs in תנ״ך, such as אז ישיר
Half-brick; here, a piece of written text
Whole brick; here, a blank space

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two bricks. Here the אריח is the written words and the לבינה is the empty space.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa said,

phrases.aramaic: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי שֵׁילָא אִישׁ כְּפַר תְּמַרְתָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Sheila of the village of Timarta taught:
All the songs are written
a half-brick over a whole brick
and a whole brick over a half-brick

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי שֵׁילָא אִישׁ כְּפַר תְּמַרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Keeps going with rules for writing the list of המן's sons, starting from the general rule for writing songs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Songs in תנ״ך are normally written with text alternating over blank space, like a well-built wall.

steps.title: המן's sons and the kings of כנען are written like a falling wall
steps.stepSummary: The exception: the list of המן's sons and the list of the kings of כנען are written with text over text and blank space over blank space. This is so that they never rise from their downfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for this song and the kings of כנען, which are written half-brick over half-brick and whole brick over whole brick. Why? So that there should be no rising up from their downfall.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רבי שילא's teaching. It gives the exception to the normal layout and explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two lists are stacked straight up: text over text, and blank over blank. One is the ten sons of המן. The other is the defeated kings of כנען in ספר יהושע. A wall built with bricks stacked straight up has no overlap, so it falls easily. The layout hints that these enemies should never recover.

keyTerms.meaning: The kings of כנען that יהושע defeated (יהושע פרק יב)

steps.whatToRemember: For המן's sons there are three rules. They are read in one breath, because they died together. The ו of ויזתא is written long, because they were hanged on one pole. Their list is written like a weak wall, so they never rise again.

phrases.english: except for this song and the kings of Canaan,
which are half-brick over half-brick
and whole brick over whole brick.
What is the reason?
So that there should be no rising up from their downfall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the exception to the general writing rule set up in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lists of המן's sons and of the kings of כנען are written like a weak wall, so that they never rise from their downfall.

steps.title: An angel slapped the king on his mouth
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that when אחשורוש began complaining about the Jews killing people in שושן, a מלאך slapped him on the mouth, so his words turned into an offer to grant אסתר's request.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And the king said to Queen אסתר: In שושן the capital the Jews have killed...' רבי אבהו said: This teaches that an angel came and slapped him on his mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a verse in which the king sounds upset at first, and רבי אבהו explains why his words suddenly change direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king starts by listing how many people the Jews killed, which sounds like a complaint. Then he suddenly asks אסתר what else she wants. רבי אבהו says a מלאך slapped him mid-sentence, so his complaint turned into a kind offer.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches (a lesson learned from the verse)

phrases.english: "And the king said to Esther the queen:
In Shushan the capital the Jews have killed..."
phrases.notes: אסתר ט:יב. The verse goes on to ask what אסתר wants.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
This teaches that an angel came
and slapped him on his mouth.
phrases.notes: So the king could not finish his complaint.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁבָּא מַלְאָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of teachings on verses near the end of the מגילה, now moving to a new verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sudden change in the king's tone came from a מלאך slapping him on his mouth.

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'he said' instead of 'she said'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a wording problem. אסתר came before the king, so the verse should say 'she said,' not 'he said.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And when she came before the king, he said with the letter.' Why 'he said'? It should have said 'she said'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the wording of a verse. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse begins with אסתר ('when she came'), so we expect it to continue with her speaking. Saying 'he said' seems to switch speakers for no reason. The גמרא wants to know what the verse means.

keyTerms.meaning: It should have said / it needed to say
Here: a letter or written decree

phrases.english: "And when she came before the king,
he said with the letter."
"He said"? It should have said "she said"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new verse and raises a wording difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'אמר' (he said) in אסתר ט:כה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse is about אסתר coming to the king, so the verb should be feminine ('אמרה').

steps.title: אסתר asked that the letter also be spoken aloud
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads the verse as אסתר's request: 'Let it be said by mouth what is written in the letter.' So the word 'אמר' is part of what she asked for.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: She said to him: Let what is written in the letter also be said out loud.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the wording problem by reading 'אמר' as part of אסתר's request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse should be read as: אסתר came and asked that 'it be said' (אמר) along with the letter. She wanted the king to announce out loud what the written decree said. So 'אמר' does not mean the king spoke. It describes what she asked for.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be said by mouth (announced out loud)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: She said to him:
Let it be said by mouth
what is written in the letter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question from step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the verse: 'אמר' is the content of אסתר's request, not the king speaking.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse seems to say the king spoke, even though it is about אסתר.
steps.terutzMaskana: אסתר asked that the written decree also be announced out loud ('יאמר'), so the verse still describes her action.

steps.title: A מגילה needs scored lines like a ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'words of peace and truth,' רבי תנחום, or some say רבי אסי, learns that a מגילה must have שרטוט (scored guide lines), just like the 'truth' of the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'words of peace and truth.' רבי תנחום said, and some say רבי אסי said: This teaches that a מגילה needs scored lines, like the truth of the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא learns a practical הלכה about how to write a מגילה from the word 'truth' (אמת) in the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אמת' (truth) is understood as a hint to the תורה, which is called truth. So the מגילה must be written like a real ספר תורה, with lines scored into the parchment before writing.

keyTerms.meaning: Scoring: lines etched into the parchment to guide the writing
Like the truth of the תורה, meaning like a real ספר תורה
And some say (a different person said it)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה: a kosher מגילה must be written on scored parchment, like a ספר תורה.

phrases.english: "Words of peace and truth."
Rabbi Tanchum said,
and some say Rabbi Asi said:
This teaches that it (the Megillah) requires scoring
like the truth of the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next verse and derives a practical הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מגילה must be written with שרטוט, like a ספר תורה.

steps.title: Did only אסתר's decree establish פורים, and not the fasts?
steps.stepSummary: The verse says 'the decree of אסתר confirmed' פורים. The גמרא asks whether this means the fasts had no part in establishing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And the decree of אסתר confirmed.' Only אסתר's decree, and not the matters of the fasts?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the plain reading of a verse that seems to give credit only to אסתר's decree. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse before this one mentions 'the matters of the fasts.' Reading verse 32 by itself suggests only אסתר's decree established פורים. But the fasts were also part of the miracle, so leaving them out seems wrong.

phrases.english: "And the decree of Esther confirmed."
"The decree of Esther," yes,
but "the matters of the fasts," no?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next verse and challenges its plain meaning.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of אסתר ט:לב that only אסתר's decree established פורים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The fasts were also part of the salvation, so they should share credit for establishing פורים.

steps.title: Read the two verses as one
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the end of verse 31 ('the matters of the fasts') and verse 32 ('the decree of אסתר confirmed these days of פורים') are read together. Both the fasts and אסתר's decree established פורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Read it as: 'The matters of the fasts ... and the decree of אסתר confirmed these days of פורים.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge by joining the two verses into one statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the verses are joined, 'the matters of the fasts' becomes part of the same sentence as 'confirmed these days of פורים.' So the fasts and אסתר's decree together established פורים. The fasts are included, not left out.
steps.whatToRemember: Several verses in this section are read in a careful way: the king was slapped by a מלאך, אסתר asked that the decree be spoken aloud, a מגילה needs שרטוט like a ספר תורה, and both the fasts and אסתר's decree established פורים.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not adding new words to the פסוק. The '...' simply shows that he joins the end of one verse to the next verse so they are read as one idea.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
"The matters of the fasts ...
and the decree of Esther confirmed
phrases.notes: Start of אסתר ט:לב, read as a continuation.

phrases.english: these (days of) Purim."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Joining verses: the two verses are read together as one statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only אסתר's decree established פורים, and the fasts were left out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fasts and אסתר's decree together established the days of פורים.

steps.title: מרדכי was accepted by most of his brothers, not all
steps.stepSummary: From the word 'most' (רוב) in the verse, the גמרא learns that some members of the סנהדרין separated from מרדכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'For מרדכי the Jew was second to King אחשורוש, great among the Jews, and accepted by most of his brothers.' It says 'most of his brothers,' not 'all of his brothers.' This teaches that some members of the סנהדרין separated from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the last verse of מגילת אסתר. It learns from the single word 'most' that not everyone was happy with מרדכי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everyone accepted him, the verse would say 'all his brothers.' Saying 'most' hints that some people stepped away. According to the commentators, they were members of the סנהדרין who felt he should not have left full-time Torah learning for a government job.

keyTerms.meaning: The High Court of Torah sages

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole next section. The idea that מרדכי lost some standing leads straight into the statements about how great תלמוד תורה is.

phrases.english: "For Mordechai the Jew
was second to King Achashverosh
and great among the Jews
and accepted by most of his brothers."
"By most of his brothers," but not by all his brothers.
This teaches that there separated from him
some members of the Sanhedrin.
phrases.notes: He was busy with community needs instead of full-time learning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the verses about establishing פורים to the closing verse of the מגילה about מרדכי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'most' shows that some of the סנהדרין separated from מרדכי.

steps.title: רב יוסף: Torah study is greater than saving lives
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that תלמוד תורה is greater than הצלת נפשות, because מרדכי dropped from fifth place to sixth place in the lists of leaders.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Torah study is greater than saving lives. At first מרדכי was listed after four people, and in the end he was listed after five.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף builds on the previous step and states a big principle. He then gives his reason: מרדכי's place in the list of leaders went down. The actual verses come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרדכי left some of his learning in order to save the Jewish people, and his ranking dropped by one place. רב יוסף reads that drop as a sign that learning Torah is on a higher level than saving lives.
steps.confusionAlert: This does NOT mean a person may ignore a life in danger in order to learn. In practice, פיקוח נפש overrides almost everything. The point here is about spiritual rank: מרדכי's standing was lowered a little because he left his learning.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Great is Torah study
more than saving lives,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא חָשֵׁיב לֵיהּ לְמׇרְדֳּכַי בָּתַר אַרְבְּעָה,
phrases.english: for at first Mordechai was counted after four,
and in the end after five.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּדוֹל תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה יוֹתֵר מֵהַצָּלַת נְפָשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea that מרדכי lost standing by turning to public affairs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תלמוד תורה is greater than הצלת נפשות.

steps.title: The two lists of leaders from עזרא and נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes both lists. In the first list מרדכי comes after four names; in the later list he comes after five.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first it is written: 'Who came with זרובבל: ישוע, נחמיה, שריה, רעליה, מרדכי, בלשן.' In the end it is written: 'Who came with זרובבל: ישוע, נחמיה, עזריה, רעמיה, נחמני, מרדכי, בלשן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the actual verses that prove רב יוסף's claim. It shows the two lists one after the other so we can count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זרובבל is the leader 'with whom' everyone came, so he is not counted. In the first list (עזרא ב) there are four names before מרדכי: ישוע, נחמיה, שריה, רעליה. In the later list (נחמיה ז) there are five: ישוע, נחמיה, עזריה, רעמיה, נחמני. So מרדכי moved down one place.

keyTerms.meaning: Leader of the return from Bavel; the others came 'with' him
The extra name added in the later list

steps.confusionAlert: Don't count זרובבל. If you count him, the numbers come out five and six instead of four and five. The others are listed as coming 'with' him.

phrases.english: At first it is written:
"Who came with Zerubavel:
Yeshua, Nechemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah,
Mordechai, Bilshan,"
phrases.notes: עזרא ב:ב. Four names before מרדכי.

phrases.english: and in the end it is written:
"Who came with Zerubavel:
Yeshua, Nechemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nachmani,
Mordechai, Bilshan."
phrases.notes: נחמיה ז:ז. Five names before מרדכי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the verses behind רב יוסף's counting claim.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that מרדכי dropped from after four to after five.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עזרא ב:ב compared with נחמיה ז:ז.

steps.title: תלמוד תורה is greater than building the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: רב (or רב שמואל בר מרתא) proves this from עזרא, who stayed in בבל to learn from ברוך בן נריה instead of going up to build the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said, and some say it was רב שמואל בר מרתא: Torah study is greater than building the בית המקדש. As long as ברוך בן נריה was alive, עזרא did not leave him to go up to ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second 'greater than' statement. This time Torah study is compared with building the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עזרא could have gone up to help build the בית המקדש, but he stayed with his teacher ברוך בן נריה to keep learning. He only went up after ברוך died. Choosing learning over building shows which one is greater.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (it was said by someone else)
Student of ירמיהו and teacher of עזרא

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא:
phrases.english: Rav said, and some say Rav Shmuel bar Marta said:

phrases.aramaic: גָּדוֹל תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה יוֹתֵר מִבִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: Torah study is greater than building the Temple,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכׇּל זְמַן שֶׁבָּרוּךְ בֶּן נֵרִיָּה קַיָּים —

steps.title: Torah study is greater than honoring parents
steps.stepSummary: רבה, quoting רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא, proves this from יעקב אבינו. He was not punished for the years he spent learning in the house of עבר. 'דאמר מר' opens the proof, which continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא: Torah study is greater than honoring one's father and mother. For all the years that יעקב אבינו was in the house of עבר, he was not punished. As the Master said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third 'greater than' statement, now comparing Torah study with כיבוד אב ואם. The step ends with 'דאמר מר,' which sets up a calculation that comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב was away from his parents for many years and could not honor them. Later he was punished by being separated from יוסף. The proof, coming next, will show that the years he spent learning with עבר were not counted in that punishment. So learning Torah outweighed honoring his parents.

keyTerms.meaning: The house (study hall) of עבר, where יעקב learned Torah
As the Master said (introduces a known teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three 'גדול תלמוד תורה' statements in a row. Torah study is greater than saving lives (from מרדכי), greater than building the בית המקדש (from עזרא), and greater than honoring parents (from יעקב).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא:
phrases.english: Rabba said that Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta said:

for all those years
that our father Jacob was in the house of Eber
he was not punished,
